finding.claim: Default SCP remote path quoting (double quotes, escaping only '"') does not stop remote shell expansion of $(...), backticks, $var, or backslashes, enabling command injection on the SSH server when the path is attacker-influenced.
finding.source: Caller-supplied remote path string passed to ScpClient upload/download (e.g. a filename from a web upload) while the default RemotePathTransformation is in effect.
finding.sink: channel.SendExecRequest("scp -t ... <transformed path>") executed by the remote shell in src/Renci.SshNet/ScpClient.cs:367 (and 410, 459, 498, 538, 578).

trace.note: Opens with '"' and appends each char; only '"' is escaped with a backslash
Closes with '"'; no handling of $, backtick, or backslash
Transformed path interpolated into scp exec command string sent to remote shell

finding.guards_checked: Default transform is DoubleQuote (insufficient). ShellQuote transform exists (RemotePathShellQuoteTransformation) and is the correct mitigation but is not the default. No validation or allowlist in ScpClient. Repro: path '/tmp/$(id)/x' expands on remote host.

finding.claim: Host key is trusted by default when no HostKeyReceived handler is attached, so the key exchange and subsequent password or key authentication proceed against any server presenting a validly self-signed host key (MITM-able).
finding.source: Network attacker positioned between client and server (or any server the client connects to), with the application not subscribing to HostKeyReceived.
finding.sink: Authentication credentials and session commands sent to an impersonated host after KeyExchange.Finish() completes.

trace.note: ValidateExchangeHash: signature checked against the presented host key, then CanTrustHostKey
CanTrustHostKey returns true when HostKeyReceived has no subscribers
Finish() throws only if ValidateExchangeHash returns false
Client wires Session.HostKeyReceived to its own event, which is null unless the application subscribes

finding.guards_checked: Exchange-hash signature verification is correct (hash computed locally, checked before NewKeys). No identity pinning or default-deny when no handler is present. Flagged explicitly per org policy as weakening authentication; may be documented intent but is the insecure default.

finding.claim: zlib decompression has no output-size cap, so a small compressed packet from a malicious server can expand to gigabytes and exhaust client memory.
finding.source: Malicious SSH server (or MITM when host keys are not verified) that negotiates zlib or zlib@openssh.com compression.
finding.sink: Unbounded MemoryStream growth in DecompressCore via _decompressor.CopyTo(outputStream) (Zlib.cs:82) and ToArray.

trace.note: Compressed packet length bounded by MaximumSshPacketSize only
Decompress dispatches to DecompressCore when active
Copies entire inflated output to MemoryStream with no limit

finding.guards_checked: Packet size cap applies to compressed input only. zlib@openssh.com is activated only after user authentication success (Compressor.cs:147-150); activation timing for plain zlib not verified.

finding.claim: A malicious SFTP server can force a large array or dictionary allocation from a single small response by sending an unvalidated element count before any entries are read.
finding.source: Malicious SFTP server response with a large Count field (uint) or extendedCount.

trace.note: Count read directly from server as uint
Array allocated at full Count before any entry is parsed
extendedCount read from server, cast to int, used as Dictionary capacity

finding.guards_checked: No comparison of count against remaining buffer length before allocation. Read loop fails later, but the allocation has already happened.

finding.claim: DH group-exchange accepts the server-supplied prime and generator without checking group size against the client's requested minimum and maximum, as required by RFC 4419 section 3.
finding.source: Malicious server or MITM sending SSH_MSG_KEX_DH_GEX_GROUP with an arbitrary prime size.
finding.sink: DHParameters constructed from server prime and generator (lines 168-173) and used for key agreement.

trace.note: DHParameters built with server values; minimum bit length only applied to private exponent

finding.guards_checked: Server signature over exchange hash (which includes p and g) is verified, limiting exploitation to cases where host key trust is also weak (see finding 2). No primality or size check on the group.
